title: First Touch Activation Checklist — Livestream AI Pilot
content:
Objective:
This doc captures the kickoff checklist, acceptance criteria, and initial workshop notes for the LiveStream AI Pilot (customer: LiveStream Inc.). The goal is a 4-week POC to demonstrate Redwood inference serving for real-time captioning + highlight extraction with predictable latency under 95th percentile SLA targets and a cost profile that can be extrapolated to production scale.

Background/context (quick):
- LiveStream Inc. wants low-latency auto-captioning and short highlight generation for user livestreams (consumer-facing).
- Customer constraints: strict startup latency (must feel 'instant'), variable concurrent stream count (50–500), sourceless media ingestion over SRT/HLS, and PII redaction requirement for chat overlays.
- Proposed Redwood approach: host a dedicated model variant for streaming generation with KV-prefix caching and a fallback smaller quantized variant for overload scenarios.

Kickoff checklist (first-touch activation):
1) Access & onboarding
   - Confirm service accounts + IAM roles for LiveStream engineering (credentials provisioned via secure link).
   - Verify sample SRT stream endpoint and representative RTMP/HLS test vectors from customer.
   - Confirm customer KMS integration requirements for Private deployment if requested.
2) Data & privacy
   - Obtain 3 sample 30–60 minute livestream recordings (anonymized) for latency/quality tests.
   - Confirm PII categories and approved redaction rules (names, emails, phone numbers).
3) Environment & infra
   - Provision dedicated inference pool (2 x A10g, autoscale allowed) in region us-west-2 for pilot.
   - Pre-warm model instances for typical concurrent stream counts (scale plan: 50, 150, 300 streams).
4) Integration & SDK
   - Deliver sample ingest adapter code (JS/Go) for LiveStream to call Redwood streaming API.
   - Validate streaming websocket handshake and chunked response behavior.
5) Observability & SLOs
   - Enable token-level and route-level tracing in Redwood Console for pilot routes.
   - Configure latency tracing dashboard and error rate alerts.
6) Acceptance test plan prepared (see below).

Success criteria (must be measurable):
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency for caption generation <= 420ms at target concurrency (150 streams).
- Throughput: System can sustain 300 concurrent streams for 20 minutes with <5% error spikes and no more than 2x baseline CPU/GPU usage above nominal.
- Quality: Word error rate (WER) <= 12% on provided sample corpus; highlight relevance precision >= 0.78 (manual eval set).
- Cost visibility: Per-stream cost estimate produced for steady-state at 150 concurrent streams (USD/hour).
- Privacy: PII redaction rules applied with 99% recall on test set (manual spot checks).
- Operational: Canary fallback to quantized variant completes within SLA (fallback time < 800ms) when primary pool is saturated.

Acceptance tests (short):
- Test A (Baseline latency): Play standardized 10-min recording to 150 parallel client emulators; measure 50/95/99 token latencies and drop rates.
- Test B (Overload/fallback): Ramp from 50 to 350 concurrent streams over 10 minutes, verify fallback triggers and end-to-end continuity.
- Test C (Quality/WER): Run ASR outputs against annotated transcripts from customer samples; compute WER and flag outlier phrases.
- Test D (PII redaction): Inject synthetic PII tokens into chat overlay, verify redaction coverage.
- Test E (Cost telemetry): Generate per-token and per-route cost reports for 24-hour simulated workload run.

Roles & responsibilities (initial):
- Solutions Lead: Maya Patel — overall POC owner, customer liaison, acceptance sign-off.
- ML Integration: Ethan Chen — model selection, quantization strategy, eval harness.
- Infra/Deploy: Rohan Mehta — infra provisioning, autoscaling, region placement.
- Observability: Samira Alvarez — dashboards, tracing, alert runbook.
- Customer Eng: Jules Park (LiveStream contact) — provide test vectors, coordinate integration week.

Timeline & milestone canvas (4-week plan):
- Week 0 (pre-kick): IAM + test vectors + infra provisioning checklist complete.
- Week 1: Streaming integration spike; connect sample ingest; baseline latency tests.
- Week 2: Quality tuning and model variant A/B tests; implement PII redaction.
- Week 3: Stress testing at scale; fallback and canary validation; cost run.
- Week 4: Final acceptance window; run acceptance tests; produce final report + production extrapolation.

Key workshop notes (initial kickoff call 2025-11-07):
- Customer emphasized user-perceived instant captions; we agreed to prioritize 95th pct token latency over raw WER during demo.
- LiveStream team will expose a test SRT endpoint and provide 3 anonymized session recordings by 11/10.
- Agreed on weekly sync cadence (Mon 09:30 PT) and ad-hoc war room during stress test windows.
- Outstanding: legal asked for sample DPIA (data protection impact assessment) before production roll; Solutions to share Redwood template.

Risks & mitigations (brief):
- Risk: Unexpected concurrent load patterns cause elevated tail latency.
  Mitigation: Pre-warm caches, use per-customer routing to regional pools, enable fast fallback variant.
- Risk: Customer data contains domain jargon that degrades quality.
  Mitigation: Quick fine-tune or prompt-set injection + eval on small in-domain corpus.
- Risk: KMS integration delays Private deployment.
  Mitigation: Run hosted pilot with strong redaction until KMS is ready; provide data handling cheat-sheet.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need clarification on whether highlight extraction must be realtime (<5s) or can be batched post-stream.
- Confirm acceptable cost ceiling for pilot (ops asked for $/stream/hr cap).
- Request sample of chat messages to evaluate PII detection false positive rate.

Deliverables by end of POC:
- Pilot results dashboard (latency, errors, cost) + runbook for production scaling.
- Acceptance report with WER and highlight precision matrices.
- Integration snippets and sample config for LiveStream infra (autoscale policy).
- Post-mortem with recommendation: Dedicated vs Shared pools and estimated monthly cost at 95% of peak.

Communication plan:
- Weekly status emails with current metrics + blockers.
- Slack channel #pilot-livestream-redwood for real-time coordination (invite sent to customer).
- Demo run at end of Week 3 for internal stakeholders; external demo after acceptance.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep runbook minimal but actionable. Add quick commands to repro fallback locally.
- Prepare short script for demo that showcases graceful degradation (show fallback in front of customers).
- Capture clip of worst-case latency for internal postmortem.

Appendix: quick checklist for first lab run:
- [ ] create service account, share secrets with LiveStream team
- [ ] upload test vectors to secure bucket and share read ACLs
- [ ] deploy model variant v1 (fp16) + variant v1-q4 (quantized)
- [ ] wire up Redwood Console dashboards and create 95th pct latency alert
- [ ] schedule stress test window and notify SRE

End of doc.
